{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"a68922218bb77e187ec52d48e6d4cbd10cf39461617f474edc157c5e11a81ba4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver condition, phones, fatigue and alcohol","heading":"C — Driver condition, phones, fatigue and alcohol","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driver condition, phones, fatigue and alcohol

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A33
According to crash records, more than 90 percent of highway crashes trace back to the driver: error, missing knowledge, inattention, physical or mental condition, a poor attitude or faulty judgment. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A33
Basic skills are not enough to make a good driver; after mastering them you must keep learning the finer points of driving and the physical and mental conditions that affect it. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A33
Family troubles, quarrels, money worries, a serious illness at home, personal fears or overconfidence can make you temporarily accident-prone, because a preoccupied mind cannot stay alert enough to drive safely. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A33
Someone who has just had a violent argument, or who is angry or grieving, needs time to cool off before driving, since venting emotions behind the wheel is very poor judgment. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A33
When you feel worried, ill, nervous, frightened, angry or depressed, the manual's advice is to let another person drive. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A33
A well-adjusted driver understands that traffic means sharing the road fairly and acts from the point of view of every road user, which the manual calls social responsibility. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A33
Good driving attitudes and sound actions show mental and emotional maturity, and that maturity matters for younger and older drivers alike. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A33
Concentration is among the most important parts of safe driving, so the driver's seat is no place for daydreaming, window shopping, sightseeing or distracting talk. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A33
Driving is a full-time job, and poor concentration dulls your observation enough to cause crashes that could have been avoided. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A34
If you use a cell phone while driving, your first responsibility is still driving the vehicle. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A34
Before making a call, size up the traffic, and know your keypad well enough to use speed dial where you can. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A34
Make calls while stopped or let a passenger place them, keep the phone within easy reach, and use a speaker phone or hands-free device. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A34
Steer clear of intense, emotional or complicated calls, avoid phone talk in heavy traffic or bad weather, and pull off the road to dial or finish a conversation. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A34
While operating a motor vehicle in Alabama, you may not use a wireless device to write, send or read texts, instant messages or e-mail. [A34]
Why it matters: reading a message is banned too, not only writing or sending one.
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A34
The manual lists texting fines of $25 for a first offense, $50 for a second and $75 for a third or later offense. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A34
Every texting offense also adds a two-point violation to the offender's driving record. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A34
Stop driving as soon as you feel drowsy instead of fighting it, and leave the highway at the first rest stop or service area. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A34
Coffee and some stretching may revive a driver who is only getting tired, but a driver who is truly sleepy should get off the highway and nap. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A34
Drowsiness is one of the biggest dangers of interstate driving, and stay-awake drugs are likely to make your driving more dangerous, not less. [A34]
Why it matters: pills are not a fix for fatigue; the manual says they add hazard.
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A34
Take a regular break every 100 miles or every two hours, getting out of the car to walk, stretch and relax. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A34
Before a long trip it is a good idea to take a nap. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A34
Highway hypnosis is drowsiness or unawareness caused by monotony, such as wind noise, tire sound on the pavement and the steady hum of the engine, and expressway drivers are prone to it. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A34
To fight highway hypnosis, keep moving your eyes across the road and focus on objects near and far, left and right; reading highway signs can also keep you alert. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A34
Your physical condition strongly affects driving ability, and alcohol, drugs, illness or disability can cause or contribute to crashes. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A34
Drinking by drivers is a major contributing factor in traffic crashes, and research shows a blood alcohol concentration of .05 percent already impairs most people's driving to some degree. [A34]
Why it matters: impairment begins well below the legal limit.
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A35
Impairment grows as blood alcohol concentration rises, and at .08 percent every person is definitely impaired. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A35
Under Alabama law it is unlawful to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of .08 percent or more, or while under the influence of alcohol. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A35
The manual reports that drinking drivers are involved in roughly 50 percent of fatal crashes each year. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

Glossary: highway hypnosis — drowsy unawareness brought on by the monotony of long expressway driving [A34]. Implied consent — the rule that driving on Alabama public highways counts as agreeing to a chemical alcohol test [A36]. Depressant — a substance such as alcohol that slows the body down rather than stimulating it [A35].
Memory aid: coffee wakes, only time sobers [A36].
